summary: Listed as a verified fire tower point in Ontario's open tower layer; no other source reached describes its history, staffing or present site.

evidence.supports: The layer lists a Louise Fire Tower
Point at about 46.3175 N, 81.3901 W (longitude first in the source)
Location placed within 50 metres of the site
The layer classes it as a fire tower
Most Ontario towers were erected between the 1920s and the 1950s, when forest fire protection was at its height
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: The site is a personal history site
evidence.quote: I decided I would produce a website to preserve the history of our fire tower lookouts and the towermen that worked them.

evidence.supports: By the 1960s the towers were used less and less as aerial spotting and firefighting took over
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

evidence.supports: A decision was made to have many towers destroyed
evidence.quote: The decision then went through to have many destroyed.

notes_for_editor: The brief gives no local_unit for this tower, so the story names only Ontario. The brief's source page (geohub.lio.gov.on.ca/datasets/mnrf::tower) has no record text in the cache, so the cited source is the LIO query response it points to, which is cached under the URL in sources[0]. The record has no height, build year, status or agency fields, and the layer's GENERAL_COMMENTS field is empty for this tower. Two searches for Louise and reads of the Firelookout.ca and Ontario hobby-site lists turned up nothing further. Unchecked leads: a Canadian Geographical Names Database entry 'Louise Tower Mountain' near Sudbury (per docs/sources/expansion_on.md; not cited because its response is not in the cache), and the 1963 tower map in data/raw/expansion/on (a scanned image). The story sits at the 120-word floor because the evidence is thin; it was not padded beyond what the sources support.
